fact_check_verdict: Core survives with hedges. Anchor is one MIT Technology Review feature (2026-10-19), cross-checked against Earth Fire Alliance (FireSat), XPRIZE, Alaska Public Media and Woodwell (Yukon Flats pilot), USFWS (acreage) and CATG. Half-of-emissions and four-percent figures date from a 2022 Woodwell-led analysis and are attributed. CUT: Canada 2023 fires (unverified), autonomous Black Hawks (California test only), any claim an AI tool is in use in Alaska fire management, any XPRIZE suppression result, Dryad company claims.

claims.spoken: Alaska makes about half of America's wildfire emissions but gets around four percent of fire money, per MIT Technology Review.
claims.on_screen: ABOUT HALF OF U.S. WILDFIRE EMISSIONS
requires: Attribute to MIT Technology Review. The figure traces to a 2022 analysis by Woodwell scientists, so never state it as a current federal number or credit a named person.
claims.verbatim_source: "While Alaska produces about half the nation's wildfire emissions, it receives around 4% of federal firefighting funds."

claims.spoken: Alaska makes about half of America's wildfire emissions but gets around four percent of fire money, per MIT Technology Review.
requires: Same attribution as c1. Pair with c1 on one plate, per MIT Technology Review.
claims.verbatim_source: "While Alaska produces about half the nation's wildfire emissions, it receives around 4% of federal firefighting funds."

claims.spoken: The Yukon Flats refuge covers about eleven million acres of wetland, forest and bog.
claims.on_screen: YUKON FLATS REFUGE · ABOUT 11 MILLION ACRES
requires: Total area. Federal ownership is 8.63 million acres, so say 'covers' and never 'federally owned'.
claims.verbatim_source: "The Yukon Flats National Wildlife Refuge is an 11-million-acre patchwork of wetlands, forests, and bogs."

claims.spoken: In twenty nineteen, fires there burned some seven hundred fifty thousand acres.
requires: Say some or about. No attribution beyond the outlet.
claims.verbatim_source: "In 2019, the region suffered a series of devastating fires that burned some 750,000 acres."

claims.spoken: On the Yukon Flats, a pilot program on one point six million acres sends crews only if they expect to contain a fire within seventy two hours.
requires: Fox is the FORMER manager. The pilot is a policy rule on 1.6 million acres, never a program that has been shown to work.
claims.verbatim_source: "persuaded managers at the US Bureau of Land Management's Alaska Fire Service to carry out a pilot project on a 1.6-million-acre section of the Yukon Flats"

claims.spoken: On the Yukon Flats, a pilot program on one point six million acres sends crews only if they expect to contain a fire within seventy two hours.
claims.on_screen: ATTACK ONLY IF CONTAINED IN 72 HOURS
requires: The 72 hours is a CONDITION for attacking a fire, never a promise or a goal that fires get contained.
claims.verbatim_source: "if they had the resources available and believed they could contain a blaze within 72 hours"

claims.spoken: Near Fairbanks, a thaw probe hits frozen ground about a foot down on unburned soil.
claims.on_screen: UNBURNED · FROZEN ABOUT A FOOT DOWN
requires: Probe by Hilary Shook, coordinator of the Alaska Fire Science Consortium, on a trail in the 2021 Yankovich Road Fire scar and just outside it. The measurement is the reporter's on-scene account.
claims.verbatim_source: "A test of the ground just outside the burn scar hit the concrete-like layer about a foot below the surface."

claims.spoken: Inside a burn scar from July of twenty twenty one, it plunged at least three times deeper.
requires: Say at least three times, never about three. The comparison is with unburned ground just outside the scar. Never claim every burn scar does this.
claims.verbatim_source: "the probe plunged at least three times deeper into the ground."

claims.spoken: One fire, in two thousand seven, released more than two million tons of carbon.
claims.on_screen: 2007 ANAKTUVUK RIVER FIRE · 2 MILLION+ TONS OF CARBON
requires: Tons of CARBON, never CO2. The fire is the 2007 Anaktuvuk River Fire. Say North Slope only if the article's place is confirmed, otherwise omit the place.
claims.verbatim_source: "it ripped across 400 square miles ... released more than 2 million tons of carbon into the air."

claims.spoken: A prototype satellite, FireSat, caught two Alaska fires in one image.
requires: FireSat is run by the nonprofit Earth Fire Alliance with Muon Space. The image is from the FireSat Protoflight, captured June 21st, 2025.
claims.verbatim_source: "This capture of the Moran Fire and Chicken Fire in one image demonstrates FireSat's value for monitoring remote regions."

claims.spoken: The aim is a scan every twenty minutes by the early twenty thirties.
requires: A GOAL for the early 2030s, never current capability. EFA's near-term target is hourly by 2029.
claims.verbatim_source: "followed by an ultimate goal of 20 minutes or less in the early 2030s."

claims.spoken: Three operational FireSats reached orbit this July.
requires: Three operational satellites, still being checked out. Never imply the constellation is complete.
claims.verbatim_source: labelled non-quotation: EFA, July 7th 2026, first three operational FireSats reach orbit

claims.spoken: In June, an X Prize contest in Alaska asked robots to find and put out a fire in ten minutes.
requires: XPRIZE Wildfire Autonomous Wildfire Response finals, June 2026, 1,000 square kilometers. Never say any team succeeded at suppression, the page does not say.
claims.verbatim_source: "autonomously detect and completely suppress a high-risk fire within 10 minutes of ignition"

claims.spoken: AURA Foresight found its fire in time.
claims.on_screen: AURA FORESIGHT · MET THE DETECTION GATE
requires: Detection only. Never say AURA or anyone suppressed a fire.
claims.verbatim_source: "successfully demonstrated autonomous and persistent detection, meeting the critical 10-minute detection gate"

requires: Track B first place, per XPRIZE. Do not say what it did on the day.
claims.verbatim_source: labelled non-quotation: XPRIZE lists Anduril Industries first place, $1.2 million, in Track B

claims.spoken: The Environmental Defense Fund says it intends to build an A I tool to pick which fires to fight.
claims.on_screen: EDF · INTENDS TO BUILD · AI TRIAGE TOOL
requires: PLANNED, NOT BUILT, and single sourced. Never say it exists, is in use, or is used in Alaska. Brian Buma, senior climate scientist, EDF.
claims.verbatim_source: "it ultimately intends to develop an AI-powered triage tool that could help fire agencies prioritize responses"

claims.spoken: A Northern Arizona University scientist says it's not clear suppression can affect these fires.
requires: Partial quote from Michelle Mack, regents professor of ecosystem ecology. Paraphrase in the VO, never put the partial words in quote marks beyond the article's.
claims.verbatim_source: "it's not clear to me that the empirical evidence suggests that we can actually have any impact on these fires"

claims.spoken: Edward Alexander of the Gwichin Council International says, we need mild fire, not wildfire.
requires: Edward Alexander, cochair of Gwich'in Council International and senior Arctic lead at Woodwell. Never link him to CATG. Spoken name respelled for the synth only.
claims.verbatim_source: "We need mild fire, not wildfire," he says.

claims.spoken: A Council of Athabascan Tribal Governments crew plans cultural burns near Fort Yukon next spring.
requires: PLANNED, per Woodwell's Brendan Rogers. Never draw it as done and never present one Native view as a bloc.
claims.verbatim_source: labelled non-quotation: MIT Technology Review, a CATG wildland crew is expected to carry out cultural burns near Fort Yukon next spring, per Brendan Rogers of Woodwell
